What is the Lumen PDF for? — One carrier example of translation rules. Not every dial plan. [cite:4]
What stays unconfirmed? — Translation syntax on a non-Cisco SBC.
Which devices does nt6eyxb include? — Desk phones except DECT and ATA, Webex App, and Local Gateway. [cite:1]
Is optimization on by default for the app? — Yes. The article says it usually needs no extra configuration. [cite:1]
Name the four phases. — Candidate discovery, candidate exchange, connectivity checks, media path optimization. [cite:1]
What minimum does that article give for CUBE? — 17.3 or 16.12.5. [cite:1]
Where does interorganization media go? — Through the PSTN. [cite:1]
What happens to a recorded call? — Media goes to the cloud and is not optimized. [cite:1]
Webex App optimized audio ports? — 8500–8599. Video is 8600–8699. [cite:3]
Device-to-device optimized ports? — 19560–19661. [cite:3]
What did September 07, 2026 change? — Phone source signaling from 5060–5080 to 5060–5280. [cite:3]
Why is SIP ALG marked re-check? — The revision line that added it is January 21, 2025, more than 12 months before 2026-10-14. The sentence is still on the page. [cite:3]
What is the August 13, 2026 NAT sentence? — Validate NAT pool size so port exhaustion does not stop users and devices. [cite:3]
What will you not teach? — A Teams media-bypass equivalent. That is unconfirmed.
What does equal priority do? — Random load balancing. [cite:1]
Define impaired. — At least one edge proxy failed. Online means all of them succeeded. [cite:1]
How often does status update? — Every 3 minutes. [cite:1]
What is error 6? — The Control Hub FQDN is missing from CN or SAN. [cite:1]
What does the london.lgw.cisco.com:5061 example prove? — The certificate must contain london.lgw.cisco.com, not the port. [cite:2]
Are wildcard certificates allowed? — t9xctu says no. [cite:3]
Does Webex require Client Authentication EKU? — No. Some third-party SBCs still reject a server-only EKU. [cite:2]
How many media PoPs is a gateway assigned? — Two, in the same region, via SRV. [cite:3]
When do errors 2, 6, 11, and 12 show? — When all edge proxy nodes have the issue. [cite:1]
What breaks above 1000 trunks in search? — You cannot sort or search within those results. [cite:1]
What is still unconfirmed? — Peer SBC priority syntax.
What does this room refuse to call estimated wait? — The labs Erlang study model.
What happens before the routing pattern runs on a skill queue? — Agents must entirely satisfy the skill requirement. [cite:1]
What clears a longest-available position? — An offer of any media type. [cite:1]
Does circular have a pointer? — Yes. Top-down does not. [cite:1]
How is a <= skill scored? — 10 minus the value. [cite:1]
Which skills are not scored? — Boolean, text, and enum. [cite:1]
Which non-skill queues does np2fdx list for Circular? — Agent assignment. [cite:1]
What is the default pattern ubg5qd names for non-skill team assignment? — Longest available. [cite:3]
Hunt-group simultaneous cap? — 50 agents. [cite:2]
What does a capacity-based team not use? — Agent Desktop. It sends voice to a DN. [cite:1]
Which Calling object provides IVR? — Auto attendant. [cite:1]
Which Calling object adds callers to a queue? — Call queue. [cite:1]
Can a hunt group take members from another location? — Yes, in the comparison table. An auto attendant cannot. [cite:1]
What does the hunt-group skill cell actually say? — Yes, not based on skills. [cite:1]
Simultaneous cap? — 50 agents. [cite:2]
What happens to member 51 when you switch to Simultaneous? — Only the first 50 are kept. [cite:2]
Non-skill team default? — Longest available. [cite:3]
Non-skill agent-assignment default? — Circular. Maximum 1,000 agents. [cite:3]
Skill patterns? — Longest available or Best available. [cite:3]
Where do you create the Contact Center queue? — Services > Contact Center > Customer experience > Queues. [cite:3]
How are CCP numbers stored? — +E.164, for DID and toll-free. [cite:2]
Is a dial plan per location? — No. It is global for the enterprise and applies to all users, regardless of location. [cite:1]
Where do Cisco Calling Plan customers open Verify Call Routing? — Services → Calling → Call Routing. Other customers use Services → PSTN & Routing → Gateway configurations. [cite:1]
What does the routing result include? — Outgoing call permissions, fraud prevention, digit patterns, call intercept, and translation patterns. [cite:1]

How do you tell CCPP media from Local Gateway media? — CCPP relays the PSTN party over the provider interconnect. Local Gateway media comes through the enterprise, from a hosted user or from enterprise PSTN. [cite:3]
Why is the PSTN caller’s receive stream blank? — Those metrics are not transmitted to the Webex Calling cloud. [cite:3]
What is LocalGatewayLoop? — A refusal: a loop between the local gateway and Webex Calling. [cite:3]

Why must contact-center phones stay out of the PSTN location? — The voice article says Cisco does not support endpoint devices in that location, and that sharing it might cause unexpected overage charges. [cite:2]
Where is the CCP country list? — The global-availability page the voice article links. “Over 65 countries” is the sentence. The page is the list, and it changes. [cite:2]
Premises-originated calls and cloud PSTN: — B. [cite:1]
A Webex Calling dial plan applies to: — B. [cite:1]

Verify Call Routing shows an outgoing-permission block. What do you edit first? — The permission the tool displayed. The refusal article lists outgoing permissions as a reject reason. Do not start by rewriting the pattern. [cite:1] [cite:3]
CCP DIDs in Control Hub are saved as: — B. [cite:2]
Off-net media through CCPP means: — B. The PSTN party’s receive metrics are not transmitted. [cite:3]
The call summary will not open the PSTN participant. What does the article say? — PSTN and Local Gateway user types are not clickable. Use the Webex participant and the hop. [cite:3]
LocalGatewayLoop is: — B. [cite:3]
Endpoint phones on the Webex Contact Center PSTN location: — B. [cite:2]
What does Flow Designer route? — Real-time calls, including how agents are assigned and what happens at each stage. [cite:1]
Can you delete Start Flow? — No. It is on the main canvas by default. [cite:1]
What is true while the validation toggle is off? — Errors do not appear, and Publish stays disabled. [cite:1]
When does Success fire on Get Queue Info? — When both EWT and PIQ are positive. [cite:1]
When does Insufficient Information fire? — PIQ is valid and EWT is −1. [cite:1]
When is EWT always −1? — Queues with team assignment and skills assigned in the flow. EWT does not apply. [cite:1]
What priority is used if the variable is 12? — 10. Only 1 through 9 are in range. [cite:1]
When is the fallback queue used? — Only if the queue variable fails to return a valid queue ID. [cite:1]
What do you insert between Queue Contact and HTTP Request? — A short delay such as Play Message or Play Music. Otherwise the request may not retrieve the data. [cite:1]
A caller dials extension 1234 and the entry point also has an E.164 number. What DNIS should the flow expect? — The E.164 number, not the extension. [cite:1]
Name both flow-opening cascades in the article. — Services → Contact Center → Flows, and Contact Center → Customer Experience → Flows. [cite:1]
What is BRE Request? — A utility activity. The Business Rules Engine user guide says a flow can invoke it. [cite:2]
With validation off: — B. [cite:1]
Start Flow: — B. [cite:1]
PIQ is 6 and EWT is −1. Which branch? — Insufficient Information. Success needs both values positive. [cite:1]
EWT on a team-assignment queue with skills assigned in the flow: — B. [cite:1]
A priority variable of 0 becomes: — C. Out of range 1–9 defaults to 10. [cite:1]

HTTP Request is the next box after Queue Contact and returns nothing. What does the article tell you to insert? — Play Message or Play Music, as a short delay, so the request can see the data. [cite:1]
Fallback queue is used when: — B. [cite:1]
Entry point has E.164 and an extension. DNIS presented to the receiving flow is: — B. [cite:1]
The article’s national-to-E.164 example is: — B. For an entry point configured with an E.164 number only. [cite:1]

A colleague says the only legal path is Services → Contact Center → Flows. What else does the same article print? — Contact Center → Customer Experience → Flows. Functions use Services → Contact Center → Customer Experience → Functions. [cite:1]
Event flows are: — B. [cite:1]
BRE Request is: — A. [cite:2]
Where do you place Callback? — After Queue Contact or Queue To Agent. [cite:1]
What does a different callback queue do to skills? — The contact goes to the end of that queue with no skills and with default priority. [cite:2]
What must exist before Schedule Callback is useful? — The Callback Default Entry Point under Channel Settings in Control Hub. [cite:2]
Which Business Hours branch wins over the shift? — Overrides and holidays, when their times coincide with the shift. Default is the leftover. [cite:1]
What is P1? — The highest static priority. P9 is the lowest. [cite:1]
A priority variable returns 15. What priority is used? — 10. Only 1 through 9 are in range. [cite:1]
Set Contact Priority is before Queue Contact, and Queue Contact also sets P5. Which one is used? — The queue activity’s priority. A later explicit priority overrides the earlier activity. [cite:2]
Why can a lower-priority Billing contact beat a higher-priority Sales contact? — Queue ranking. Billing is offered first while it still has waiting contacts. [cite:2]
How many callback retries, and over what span? — Up to 10 attempts across 14 days. Each Wait is between 10 seconds and 72 hours. [cite:2]
Where does Call Progress Analysis go on a scheduled callback? — It can be placed after NewPhoneContact in the main flow. Courtesy callback can place it after Callback. [cite:2]
Callback belongs: — B. [cite:1]

The callback is sent to a different queue. What happens to skills and place in line? — End of the selected queue, no skills, default priority. The original queue would have kept position, skills, and priority. [cite:2]
For best results, immediately after Schedule Callback the article recommends: — B. [cite:2]
Static priority P9 is: — B. P1 is highest. Unset priority is 10, which is outside P1–P9. [cite:1]

Billing is ranked above Sales. Sales holds an older P1 contact. Billing holds a P9 contact. Who does Team A get first? — The Billing contact, while Billing still has waiting contacts. Queue ranking is applied before that priority comparison. [cite:2]
A holiday that falls inside the shift takes: — B. Holidays win regardless of the shift when today is on the holiday list. [cite:1]
Agent-assignment overflow on a timer: — B. Timed target expansion is the team-queue call distribution group. [cite:2]

Call Progress Analysis is after Callback on a personal scheduled callback. Where can the article place it instead? — It can be placed after NewPhoneContact in the main flow. After Callback is a placement the article names for courtesy callback. [cite:2]
What is Webex Connect? — A programmable CPaaS with APIs, SDKs, and low-code tools, organized as six areas. [cite:1]
What is a service? — The workspace for assets, integrations, credentials, flows, and rules. [cite:1]
Which assets does the page put in Control Hub? — Email and Chat. Other channels have portal docs. [cite:1]
Inbound versus outbound webhook? — Inbound starts a flow or a rule. Outbound delivers receipts and incoming messages. [cite:1]
What is a Task? — Agent work. A call, a chat session, or an email chain. [cite:2]
Which scopes list tasks? — cjp:config or cjp:config_read. [cite:2]
Which recording events can you name? — recordingStarting, recordingStarted, recordingPaused, recordingResumed, recordingStopped, on telephony_calls. [cite:3]
What scope do those recording events use? — spark-admin:calls_read. [cite:3]
Why is serviceType required? — List Events requires it when the resource is convergedRecordings. [cite:3]
Is Flow Builder the same canvas as Flow Designer? — No. Flow Designer is T8-R01. Flow Builder is Connect. [cite:1]
Where is the subscription limit? — Webhooks guide, retrieved 2026-10-14: 30000 personal per user, and org-wide limit 1 with extra registrations per resource and filter. [cite:6]
Can the Salesforce gadget show the WhatsApp thread? — No. CRM connectors exclude chat and email. Connect holds the digital channel. [cite:4]
What does the connector launch? — Desktop, from inside Salesforce, Dynamics, or ServiceNow. [cite:1]
Which channels are excluded? — Chat and email, on every CRM integration that uses these connectors. [cite:1]
Which Salesforce editions qualify? — Development, Enterprise, and Ultimate. Group and Professional do not. [cite:1]
Is Salesforce Classic supported? — No. Lightning from App Manager. [cite:1]
Which browsers does Salesforce name for WebRTC? — Firefox and Google Chrome. Edge is not supported. [cite:1]
Which browsers does Dynamics name for WebRTC? — Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome. [cite:2]
When is CIF 2 required? — Multi-session apps, such as Omnichannel for Customer Service or Customer Service Workspace. A single-session app such as Customer Service Hub uses CIF 1. [cite:2]
What does Validate using Dial Plans do inside the gadget? — Nothing in the current gadget. The article says the setting has no effect. [cite:1]
Which timeout logs the connector out? — A custom Desktop Profile Desktop Timeout. The tenant Desktop Inactivity Timeout does not. [cite:1]
Which campaign fields does Salesforce require? — CAMPAIGN_CRM_ID. FirstName and LastName are optional. The modes are Predictive and Progressive. [cite:1]
What extra campaign field do Dynamics and ServiceNow require? — CAMPAIGN_CRM_TABLE, along with CAMPAIGN_CRM_ID. [cite:2] [cite:3]
What happens when a Dynamics screen pop sends both recordType and crmId? — The defined URL is ignored. The URL must be relative to open a Dynamics record. [cite:2]
Why can the same agent fail WebRTC in Edge on one CRM and succeed on another? — Salesforce and ServiceNow say Edge is not supported. Dynamics names Edge and Chrome. [cite:1] [cite:2] [cite:3]
Chat inside the Salesforce gadget is: — B. [cite:1]
Salesforce Classic is: — B. [cite:1]
Salesforce WebRTC in Microsoft Edge is: — B. Firefox and Chrome are the named browsers. [cite:1]
Dynamics WebRTC names: — B. [cite:2]
Omnichannel for Customer Service is the app. Which CIF version does the article require? — CIF 2. CIF 1 is the single-session app, such as Customer Service Hub. [cite:2]
On-premises Dynamics is: — B. [cite:2]
Validate using Dial Plans is selected in Control Hub. What does the gadget do with that list? — Nothing. The current gadget does not check or restrict the DN from that list. [cite:1]

The tenant Desktop Inactivity Timeout is set. What does that setting do to the connector? — It does not log the connector out. Configure a custom Desktop Profile Desktop Timeout when you want that logout. [cite:1]
Salesforce campaign identification requires: — A. Dynamics and ServiceNow add CAMPAIGN_CRM_TABLE. [cite:1] [cite:2]
A Dynamics screen pop includes both recordType and crmId. What happens to the URL? — The defined URL is ignored. The URL that opens a Dynamics record is relative. [cite:2]
Is AI Assistant a Flow Designer activity? — No. It is a paid desktop add-on with an icon. [cite:1]
Name four Assistant features. — Summaries, wellness breaks, real-time transcripts, Real-Time Assist. Also Auto CSAT, sentiment, and Topic Analytics. [cite:1]
Where are scripted and autonomous agents built? — AI Agent Studio. [cite:3]
Which products can use them? — WxCC, WxCCE, UCCE, PCCE, and UCCX (Alpha), for both scripted and autonomous, as that table prints. [cite:3]
How do you attach one to a voice flow? — Virtual Agent V2. Choose Webex AI Agent Scripted or Autonomous and a published agent. [cite:2]
What are the VAV2 outcomes? — Handled, Escalated, Errored. [cite:2]
How do you override language? — Set Global_Language, for example fr-CA, before the activity. Global_VoiceName overrides the voice. [cite:2]
Which digital channels does the integration article name? — WhatsApp, SMS, Email, Facebook Messenger, Apple Messages for Business, Live Chat. As of 2026-10-14. [cite:2]
Where do custom events work? — Voice only, for scripted and autonomous agents. [cite:2]
What must you not upload? — PCI, PII, PHI, and other sensitive or regulated information. [cite:3]

What is the Connect node timeout? — s0qro1 names onTimeOut when the agent hasn’t responded in not more than 15 seconds. The node-outcomes list on that page does not print a timer field. Read that list before you teach a timeout you can set. [cite:2]

How is the add-on ordered, in the Studio guide’s words? — AI Agent units under the Collaboration Flex 3.0 Contact Center offering. Digital agents activate with the voice subscription. Do not invent a part number. [cite:3]
When does the call show up? — After it ends. [cite:1]
Which roles? — Full admin, read-only admin, support admin. [cite:1]
Name the three statuses. — Successful, Refusal, Failure. [cite:1]
Name the quality grades. — Poor, Good, None / Not available. [cite:1]
What ties Alice’s two segments? — The correlation ID. [cite:1]
Online versus impaired? — All proxies, versus at least one. [cite:2]
Which errors need every proxy? — 2, 6, 11, and 12. [cite:2]
What does validation refuse to grade? — The PSTN and PBX dial plan. [cite:3]
How long are validation results kept? — Two years. Config data leaves after 8 hours. [cite:3]
What does DS 64224 do at 75 percent? — Disables all debugs and uninstalls diagnostic signatures. [cite:4]
What is still unmarked? — QM retention and any client-log window this pass did not open.
What JSON file is on the details page? — The call report. [cite:1]
What else is on that page? — Participant details as CSV. [cite:1]
Which phones does the PRT overview name? — WxC MPP phones and DECT base stations. [cite:2]
Online MPP action? — Report Problem. [cite:2]
DECT menu path? — Management > Devices, then Support, Manage. [cite:2]
Why can a base refuse a remote PRT? — No connected handset, so no SIP registration. [cite:2]
Where are DECT PRTs stored? — Under the base station’s device ID. [cite:2]
Two logging levels? — Standard and Debug. [cite:3]
How wide is Debug? — The entire DECT network. [cite:3]
When may bases restart? — When applying a logging change that also has other queued configuration. [cite:3]
What needs a re-check or is unconfirmed? — The July 01, 2025 PRT page. App client log retention. status.xml counts were omitted.
Which page restricts Cisco Calling Plan toll-free? — g1gtsdb. [cite:2]
Name two October 2026 Calling items. — DECT logging on October 13. The country list on October 7. [cite:1]
Who can receive a virtual line on September 24? — Eligible Cisco-managed third-party phones. Not ATAs or DECT handsets. [cite:1]
What did star do before September 23? — It could open the voice portal during deposit and lock the mailbox. [cite:1]
Toll-free on Cisco Calling Plan, which locations? — U.S. and Canada. [cite:2]
License name? — BCIBTFTN. [cite:2]
AutoCSAT value source? — The system. Not a hand-entered agent value. [cite:3]
Export length? — Up to 36 months, beyond the 13-month window, when extended retention is enabled. [cite:3]
Default routing for existing WhatsApp flows? — Webex Connect Flow Builder. [cite:3]
Agent media types on the October 6 page? — Voice, Chat, Email, and Social. [cite:4]
When is granular state optional? — Until October 29, 2026. [cite:4]
W70 version and the user action? — 146.87.254.37. Reboot after the maintenance date or wait for Thursday morning local resync. [cite:6]
